To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Li diffusion coefficients of β-LiAl are anomalously high and the Li diffusivities of β-LiIn are anomalously low at the Li-rich composition.
the Li diffusion coefficient in the β-LiAl, β-LiGa, and β-Li-In compounds is strongly affected by the formation of Li vacancy and the interaction between Li vacancy and other defects.
the Li diffusion coefficient in the β-LiAl compound is anomalously high at the composition of Li-rich side, while that of the β-LiIn compound is high at the composition near the stoichiometry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the novel method of the radioactive tracer diffusion, and the diffusion of Li in Li intermetallic compounds.
the development of a novel method to investigate the composition-dependent diffusion in solid solutions, and the diffusion mechanism of Li in β-LiAl, β-LiIn and β-LiGa.
a novel aspect of Li diffusion in β-type Li intermetallices, which may be related to the Li diffusion in the β-LiAl-based solid electrolyte.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the diffusion of Li in β-LiAl is controlled by the concentration of Li interstitials, while that of Li in βLiGa is governed by the concentration of vacancies, which is in contrast to the diffusion of Li and Ga in β-LiIn.
the Li diffusion in the NaT1-type Li intermetallicity of β-LiAl, β-LiGa, and β-LiGaIn is strongly affected by the defect formation.
Li diffuses abnormally in Li-deficient β-LiGa because of the formation of a defect complex, which has not been found in other β-LiM (M: Al, In).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diffusion of Li is controlled not only by the concentration of the Li-vacancy but by the formation of a defect complex.
Li diffusion in the β-LiAl, β-LiGa, and β-LiGaIn is controlled by the interaction between the intrinsic constitutional defects and the extrinsic defects, such as Li interstitial and vacancies.

the Li diffusion coefficients in NaTl-type intermetallic compounds are determined by the formation of Li interstitial-vacancy defect complexes and the interactions between the defects, and that the defect formation energies are strongly dependent on the chemical species of the host metal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diffusion coefficient of Li in Li-poor β-LiGa is much larger than that of Li-rich β-LiGa, and the diffusion coefficient in Li-poor composition is comparable to that of the iso-structural LiAl.

the Li diffusion in the Li-rich intermetallic compound β-LiGa is strongly influenced by the defect complex, and the Li diffusion in Li-poor composition is dominated by the defect complex formation and the interaction between defects.   1
the diffusion of Li in the β-LiAl-type intermetallic compounds should be treated as the diffusion of Li through the formation of defect complexes.
